market_context: United States and Canada; practical, safety-first household guidance written natively for North American readers.
title: How Long Can Cooked Chicken Sit Out?

seo.title: How Long Can Cooked Chicken Sit Out?
seo.meta_description: Cooked chicken should generally not stay unrefrigerated for more than about two hours, or about one hour in very hot conditions. Reheating does not reset that history.
seo.search_intent: Decide whether cooked chicken left at room temperature is still safe based on elapsed time and ambient heat.

excerpt: Cooked chicken is still perishable. If it sits on the table for hours, reheating later does not automatically make it safe again.
content_html:
As a practical rule, refrigerate cooked chicken within about two hours. When the surrounding temperature is above roughly 90°F (32°C), shorten that to about one hour.

Count from the time temperature control ended

At a meal, buffet, or cookout, add up the time chicken spends warm. Food held continuously at a safe hot temperature is different from chicken sitting lukewarm on a table.

Divide leftovers for fast cooling

Use shallow containers rather than one large, dense pile. That helps the refrigerator cool the center quickly.

Reheating is not a reset button

Some bacteria can produce toxins that are not solved simply by heating the food later. If chicken sat out too long, discard it.

Appearance and smell are not safety tests

Chicken can look and smell normal even after spending too long at an unsafe temperature.

For a long meal, put out smaller portions

If chicken will be served over an extended period, keep the reserve properly chilled or held safely hot and replenish smaller amounts. Setting out the entire tray at the beginning makes it difficult to know how long each portion has spent at an unsafe temperature.

If you cannot tell whether it was out for two hours or most of the afternoon, treat the time as unknown and choose the safer option.

faq.question: Can I eat chicken that sat out for three hours?
faq.answer: Standard guidance is to discard perishable food that exceeded about two hours at room temperature.

faq.question: Will reheating it thoroughly make it safe?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Reheating does not undo every risk created during prolonged warm storage.

faq.question: What if it was on a warming tray?
faq.answer: Food held continuously at a verified safe hot-holding temperature is different from food left lukewarm.
